ANALYSES_FROZEN.B_stage_tracing: classify every required_evidence_id of every task, every scale, into exactly one R-code; report the percentage distribution
ANALYSES_FROZEN.C_hop_ceiling: P(required record reachable within h hops), h in {1,2,3,4,unlimited}, using DIAGNOSTIC unbounded BFS over the SAME current edge set -- no production hop change. Answers whether MAX_HOPS=2 is too shallow (curve keeps rising past h=2) vs whether the topology itself is missing edges (curve flattens by h=2-3)
ANALYSES_FROZEN.D_identity_fragmentation_ceiling: reachability under the CURRENT raw-surface-normalized graph vs a diagnostic graph where nodes are merged using oracle latent identity (latent_subject/latent_bridge) instead of runtime surface normalization -- isolates how much headroom exists in canonicalization specifically
ANALYSES_FROZEN.E_topology_ceiling: reachability under a diagnostic graph built ONLY from oracle proof_edges (task._oracle_metadata.proof_edges), restricted to records/entities already inside the SAME candidate pool (never adding records retrieval didn't find) -- isolates how much headroom exists in edge/relation-type richness specifically, never exposed to any runtime mechanism

MECHANICAL_DECISION.R3_share_and_topology_ceiling: 5.7% share, and oracle relation topology only reaches 56.6% (well below the 87.1% identity-merge ceiling) -- richer edge types are NOT yet justified
MECHANICAL_DECISION.R4_share_and_hop_curve: 4.2% share, and the hop curve is nearly flat past h=1 -- deeper traversal is NOT justified without further evidence
MECHANICAL_DECISION.conclusion: R0 (retrieval availability) is real but secondary (7.3%) -- graph-guided seed retrieval is NOT the next sprint
MECHANICAL_DECISION.decision: G2-v4 (next sprint, not started): repair entity canonicalization / graph-node merging. Specifically target identity-role alias resolution (100% genuine fragmentation, the runtime's own extract_identity_links/alias_links mechanism exists for exactly this and is under-performing) and terminal-role surface-form merging (68.4% genuine fragmentation).
MECHANICAL_DECISION.rule_applied: if R2 dominates: repair entity canonicalization / graph-node merging (frozen in configs/gate_g2_v3_reachability_v1.json BEFORE this ran)

hop_ceiling.meaning: Nearly FLAT past h=1 (+1.3pp from h=1 to h=2, +5.5pp total from h=2 to unlimited). Confirms deeper traversal is NOT the answer: the topology is missing NODES (via fragmentation) far more than it is missing HOPS. Matches the user's own worked counterexample exactly.

identity_fragmentation_ceiling.meaning: If entity canonicalization/graph-node merging were perfect, reachability would rise from 30.2% to 87.1% -- the single largest, cleanest lever identified across the entire B4/G1/G2/G2-v2/G2-v3 sequence.

topology_ceiling.meaning: Secondary lever. Even a perfect oracle relation-topology layer only reaches 56.6% chain-reachability -- well below the 87.1% identity-merge ceiling -- so typed relation edges (OWNED_BY/DEPENDS_ON/etc) are NOT yet justified as the next investment; canonicalization is the higher-leverage, cleaner target.
topology_ceiling.note_this_is_LOWER_than_pool_membership_: Oracle topology requires the FULL proof chain's records to be jointly present in the pool, not just the specific record being checked -- so it is stricter than raw per-record pool membership, and correctly shows that even perfect relation-typed edges are capped by chain-completeness of retrieval, not just by edge-type richness.

headline_finding.meaning: Required evidence overwhelmingly fails to reach S2 not because it's unretrieved (R0=7.3%), not because it's structurally distant (R4 >2-hop=4.2%), not because ranking/completion mis-scores it once found (R6+R7=6.8%), but because the SAME real-world entity is represented as different, unmerged graph nodes depending on which surface form (canonical, abbreviation, alias) a given record happens to use.

r2_subclassification.conclusion: The dominant failure is real, not a diagnostic or extraction artifact. Identity-role records (surface->canonical mapping records, e.g. 'JPA-5 is the short code for X') are 100% genuine fragmentation by construction -- their entire purpose is to state a DIFFERENT surface form, and the runtime's own alias-resolution mechanism (extract_identity_links -> graph.alias_links) is failing to connect most of them into the subject's component despite existing for exactly this purpose.
r2_subclassification.purpose: Distinguish extraction-boundary noise (cheap fix: extract_v4_entities' greedy regex over/under-captures the SAME mention) from genuine cross-surface fragmentation (structural: alias/abbreviation with zero textual overlap, requires real canonicalization/node-merging work) -- added mid-sprint before freezing the conclusion, since a 60%+ R2 rate on terminal records could plausibly have been mostly the former.

what_survives_from_this_sprint: scripts/diagnose_g2_v3_reachability.py: the R0-R8 stage tracer, hop-ceiling curve, identity-fragmentation ceiling, and topology ceiling -- all evaluator-only diagnostics, reusable for validating whatever canonicalization repair comes next

the mechanical decision rule was frozen before any number was seen, and fired cleanly on the first try -- R2 dominance, low R0/R3/R4, flat hop curve, and the identity ceiling all independently point the same direction

MECHANICAL_DECISION_RULE_FROZEN_BEFORE_R.dominance_definition: the R-code accounting for the largest share of non-R8 required-record failures, pooled across all five scales -- not decided per-scale, since a mechanism choice needs to generalize
MECHANICAL_DECISION_RULE_FROZEN_BEFORE_R.if_R0_dominates: build graph-guided retrieval / seed expansion -- the graph is being blamed for evidence it never received
MECHANICAL_DECISION_RULE_FROZEN_BEFORE_R.if_R3_dominates_and_oracle_topology_ceil: add runtime typed relation edges (OWNED_BY/DEPENDS_ON/etc) -- only after proving via the E ceiling that those edges would actually connect the missing paths
MECHANICAL_DECISION_RULE_FROZEN_BEFORE_R.if_R3_dominates_but_oracle_topology_ceil: the corpus's proof relations themselves don't route through any co-mention-adjacent structure; a richer edge ontology alone would not fix it -- distinct, harder problem
MECHANICAL_DECISION_RULE_FROZEN_BEFORE_R.if_R4_dominates_and_hop_curve_keeps_risi: test bounded deeper traversal (only after this measurement, never assumed)
MECHANICAL_DECISION_RULE_FROZEN_BEFORE_R.if_R6_dominates: fix the path enumerator (should be near-zero given current enumerate_paths logic; a nonzero rate here is itself informative)
MECHANICAL_DECISION_RULE_FROZEN_BEFORE_R.if_R7_dominates: revisit endpoint semantics -- already shown unlikely by G2-v2's K3 result, kept as a named branch for completeness rather than assumed impossible

R0_R8_TAXONOMY_FROZEN.R0_NOT_IN_CANDIDATE_POOL: required record id not in the C2 fused top-k pool for this task
R0_R8_TAXONOMY_FROZEN.R1_ENTITY_EXTRACTION_MISSING: record is in the pool but extract_v4_entities() finds zero entities in its content
R0_R8_TAXONOMY_FROZEN.R2_IDENTITY_FRAGMENTED: an entity IS extracted, and the oracle-true canonical surface (task._oracle_metadata.surfaces) IS textually present in the record, but no extracted entity normalizes to match that oracle canonical surface -- the graph node this record produces does not connect back under the runtime's own normalization
R0_R8_TAXONOMY_FROZEN.R3_DISCONNECTED_COMPONENT: the entity is extracted and DOES match the oracle canonical surface, a graph node exists, but BFS from the subject over the current edge set (unlimited hops) never reaches it -- collapses the user's originally separate R3/R5 codes, see note above
R0_R8_TAXONOMY_FROZEN.R4_REQUIRES_GT2_HOPS: reachable in the same connected component, but shortest-path hop distance from the subject exceeds the frozen production MAX_HOPS=2 bound
R0_R8_TAXONOMY_FROZEN.R6_REACHABLE_BUT_NOT_ENUMERATED: hop distance <= 2, but the record never appears in any PathCandidate produced by the real, unmodified enumerate_paths()
R0_R8_TAXONOMY_FROZEN.R7_ENUMERATED_NOT_COMPLETED: appears in a PathCandidate, but that path's complete flag is False under K1 (the validated entity-bound recognizer)
R0_R8_TAXONOMY_FROZEN.R8_COMPLETE: reachable, enumerated, and completed -- no defect at this record for this mechanism stage
R0_R8_TAXONOMY_FROZEN.note: Applied per required_evidence_id per task, first-failing-stage wins. R3 and the user's originally proposed R5 (NO_RUNTIME_EDGE_PATH) collapse to one code: being in a different connected component under the current edge set (BFS over ENTITY_LINKED_TO_ENTITY + alias edges, unlimited hops) IS the definition of 'no runtime edge path exists' -- a genuinely reachable-at-some-hop node is by definition in the same component, so a separate 'same component but no path' bucket is not logically distinct once hop count is measured separately as R4. Recorded here explicitly so this collapse is a stated design decision, not silent renumbering.

evaluator_only_diagnostic_boundary.rule: This sprint reads task['_oracle_metadata'] (surfaces, proof_edges, latent_subject, latent_bridge, answer_node) directly -- that is legitimate HERE because this is a pure analysis script that never feeds anything back into a runtime mechanism, unlike K3 (oracle_endpoint_ceiling.py) which is itself an SCORED arm gated by the runtime leakage wall. The distinction: K3 produces a completion_fn callable that could in principle be wired into g2_paths.py (and is barred from doing so only by the import-boundary test); this sprint produces a report, nothing callable, nothing importable by runtime code.

frozen_hypotheses.H1_retrieval_availability: the required bridge/endpoint record is not even in C2's candidate pool
frozen_hypotheses.H2_entity_fragmentation: the record is in the pool, but the same real-world entity appears under incompatible surface/canonical nodes, so the graph is disconnected
frozen_hypotheses.H3_topology_edge_construction: records and entities are present and correctly canonicalized, but the corpus expresses the chain through a relationship co-mention edges cannot represent

frozen_unchanged_this_sprint: no mechanism promoted or rejected by this sprint -- diagnosis only
objective: Why is required evidence absent from the runtime graph neighborhood? No mechanism modification. Diagnostic only.
why_this_sprint: G2-v2's K3 oracle endpoint ceiling showed only 0.0-0.013 absolute headroom over K0 on working-set CES at every scale -- even a PERFECT completion recognizer, restricted to the current graph topology, could not meaningfully improve the working set. That falsifies 'recognition is the bottleneck' and narrows the diagnosis one layer earlier: the graph generally does not put required evidence on a reachable path in the first place. This sprint decomposes WHY, across three independent hypotheses, before any mechanism is touched.
